topicName: Application Servers (Puma, Unicorn) and Thread Safety
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Ruby on Rails Application Servers and Thread Safety"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When deploying a Ruby on Rails application, choosing the right application server and understanding thread safety is critical for performance, resource utilization, and stability. This tutorial explores Puma and Unicorn, the two most popular Rails application servers, and how to write thread-safe code."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Application Server Architecture: Puma vs. Unicorn"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Unicorn is a multi-process application server. It follows a pre-fork worker model where a master process spawns multiple worker processes. Each worker process handles one request at a time. If you want a Unicorn server to handle 16 concurrent requests, you must boot 16 heavy worker processes, which can consume a significant amount of RAM."},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"Puma, on the other hand, uses a concurrent architecture combining processes and threads. Puma spawns multiple worker processes, and each worker runs a thread pool. This allows a single worker process to handle multiple requests simultaneously using threads. Puma is generally more memory-efficient and faster for modern Rails applications."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Puma for Concurrency"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Puma is configured through the config/puma.rb file. Here is a production-ready configuration that utilizes both workers (processes) and threads:"},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"max_threads_count = ENV.fetch('RAILS_MAX_THREADS') { 5 }
min_threads_count = ENV.fetch('RAILS_MIN_THREADS') { max_threads_count }
threads min_threads_count, max_threads_count

worker_timeout ENV.fetch('TIMEOUT') { 3600 }

port ENV.fetch('PORT') { 3000 }
environment ENV.fetch('RAILS_ENV') { 'development' }

workers ENV.fetch('WEB_CONCURRENCY') { 2 }

preload_app!

plugin 'tmp_restart'"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"What is Thread Safety?"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Thread safety means that your code can safely execute across multiple threads concurrently without data corruption, race conditions, or unexpected behavior. In a single-threaded environment like standard Unicorn, global variables or class-level instance variables might seem safe. However, in a multi-threaded server like Puma, multiple threads share the same process memory space."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Thread Safety Pitfalls in Ruby"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Global variables ($global_var) and Class-level instance variables (@class_variable) shared across requests can be modified concurrently by different threads, leading to race conditions."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Non-thread-safe third-party gems that hold internal state without synchronization mechanisms."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Lazy loading constants in multi-threaded environments can sometimes cause deadlock issues if multiple threads attempt to load the same constant simultaneously."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Writing Thread-Safe Rails Code"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"To ensure your application is thread-safe, avoid mutating global or class-level state. Instead, rely on instance variables within controller actions or service objects, which are instantiated per request."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"# Unsafe: Using a class-level variable
class AnalyticsService
  @@total_requests = 0

  def self.track
    @@total_requests += 1 # Race condition risk!
  end
end

# Safe: Using local variables or thread-safe synchronization
class ThreadSafeAnalyticsService
  @@mutex = Mutex.new
  @@total_requests = 0

  def self.track
    @@mutex.synchronize do
      @@total_requests += 1
    end
  end
end"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Database Connections and Thread Pools"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Active Record automatically checks out a database connection from the pool for each thread. If your Puma server has 5 threads per worker, ensure your database pool size in config/database.yml matches or exceeds that number to prevent thread starvation."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"production:
  adapter: postgresql
  encoding: unicode
  pool: <%= ENV.fetch('RAILS_MAX_THREADS') { 5 } %>
  database: my_app_production
  username: my_app
  password: <%= ENV['MY_APP_DATABASE_PASSWORD'] %>"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Migrating to Puma and enabling multi-threading can greatly enhance your Rails application performance while reducing memory usage. Always audit your code, gems, and database connection pool configurations to ensure complete thread safety before launching to production."}]
